newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl critic warns German CDU against smugness.
newsitem.headline: Kohl critic warns German CDU against smugness.

text.p: An up-and-coming young leader in Helmut Kohl's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) warned the party on Wednesday it could not expect to win reelection just because the veteran chancellor had decided to run again.

Christian Wulff, who earlier this year openly criticised Kohl for not pushing tax reform through faster, told Stern magazine Kohl would not win support among young voters just on the strength of his foreign policy.

"It's right for him to take foreign policy very very importantly," said Wulff, 37, opposition leader in the Lower Saxony state assembly and a leading figure among an outspoken new CDU generation known as "the wild young ones."
"But my generation is not as massively worried about foreign policy as the generation that went through the war. We younger people think European integration can no longer be seriously threatened."
Kohl, 67, announced this month he wanted to run for an unprecedented fifth term in late 1998.
The decision ended weeks of speculation about Kohl's waning influence in the party that began after Wulff openly criticised him without being called back into line.
Wulff said Kohl still enjoyed support and trust among voters but added: "His decision is still no guarantee of success in 1998. We now have to turn towards domestic reforms."
